fix.failing_test_first:
The test is scripts/app-icon.test.ts in the root unit suite (14 cases). It decodes PNGs with Node's zlib and adds no dependency. It reads each app's tauri.conf.json bundle.icon list: every PNG, every PNG frame inside icon.ico (16/24/32/48/64/256) and every PNG entry inside icon.icns. It also reads every PNG in both icons folders and the 15 Android mipmap launcher PNGs. It asserts the design: the centre pixel is dark mahogany (opaque, r 90-200, g and b at most 80, r at least 2g). A pixel just inside each of the four edges (4% inset) is tan or cream. The four corners are transparent (alpha under 32, because resampling leaves alpha 3-4 at 16/32 px; a square tile would be 255). No file in either icons folder or the mipmaps has the sha256 of a stock file; the stock hashes are pinned in the test because the script tests don't use git. Each icons folder holds exactly its 16 files, and each mipmap folder its 3. apps/ui/index.html has <link rel="icon" type="image/svg+xml" href="/favicon.svg">, and apps/ui/public/favicon.svg is byte-identical to the master. The master's sha256 is pinned too: if it changes, the test says to regenerate.

Red on base 822f142 (`flock /tmp/frbench/heavy.lock pnpm vitest run --project unit scripts/app-icon.test.ts`): Tests 9 failed | 5 passed (14). The 5 that passed: the master pin, 'lists the PNGs, the .ico and the .icns' x2 and 'same files as before' x2.

fix.update_log_suggestion:
U-NNN (open; fixed by fix/app-icon e049cf1, c682a4a, eae564a): Every app showed Tauri's stock icon (yellow and blue rings): the installer, the taskbar, the Start menu, the tray, the window, the Android launcher, and no icon at all in the UI's browser tab. Action: the owner's confirmed design of 2026-11-18 (docs/design/icon/forerunner-icon.svg, a mahogany cut-stone kite on a crisp rounded cream-to-tan tile) is rendered in Chromium and turned into every icon set with `tauri icon`. The UI gets the master as an SVG favicon. scripts/app-icon.test.ts failed on 822f142 and passes now. Check in the app: install the MSI from the Desktop app workflow run of this commit over the current version. During setup and in Apps & features the installer shows the red kite on the cream-to-tan tile. After the install, the desktop shortcut, the Start menu entry and the taskbar button while the app runs all show it, as does the window's title bar. The tray icon shows the kite too. Start a session on a project and the tray icon gets the blue dot with a white ring at its lower right; when the session ends the dot goes away. On Linux, check the AppImage/.deb launcher and the tray. On Android, install the APK: the home-screen and app-drawer icon shows the kite on the tile (round launchers: the tile in a circle). In the browser (pnpm --filter @forerunner/ui dev, http://localhost:1420), the tab shows the kite.

I looked at each file with the Read tool, enlarged by nearest-neighbour so the pixels show; the enlarged copies are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/9d17d664-b8c3-5e0d-8f13-1f917f72dcc2/scratchpad/icon/.

- The 1024 px Chromium render matches the master: an eight-facet mahogany cut-stone kite with a lighter red upper-left facet and very dark lower-right facets. It sits on a rounded square fading from pale cream in the middle to tan at the edges, and the corners outside the rounding are transparent.
- 16 px (the icon.ico frame): still reads as a red diamond/kite on a tan tile. The bright top-left facet and the dark lower half are visible as separate blocks; the corners are grey in the preview, so they are see-through. Pixels: centre rgb(142,42,36), top edge rgb(205,185,147), corner alpha 3.
- 32 px (32x32.png, the Linux window and tray icon): a clean kite shape with the light upper facets and dark lower facets clearly apart, on the cream-to-tan tile with rounded corners. Centre rgb(135,39,34), top edge rgb(199,174,135), corner alpha 3-4.
- 256 px (the icon.ico frame): crisp, like the master, with every facet edge sharp, the thin outline visible and a smooth radial fade.
- icon.png at 512 px: centre rgb(131,37,33), corner alpha 0.
- Android: ic_launcher shows the rounded tile with a small margin, ic_launcher_round the tile masked to a circle with the kite whole, and ic_launcher_foreground the full tile.
- Tray running dot: I drew the dot over the new 32x32.png exactly as with_running_dot does (radius 22% of the size, a white ring of 6%, at the lower right). The blue disc with its white ring stands out clearly from the tan tile and the dark kite, and it covers the kite's lower-right facets and tip area without hiding the shape. It reads well against both a light and a dark tray background.

non_blocking: The 'same bytes' claim is not quite true for icon.icns. docs/maintainers/apps.md ('The app icon': 'apps/desktop/src-tauri/icons and apps/mobile/src-tauri/icons (the same bytes)'), the e049cf1 commit body and the fixer's report all say it. 15 of the 16 files match byte for byte. icon.icns does not (sha256 d55e0558... vs 415df73a...): `tauri icon` writes the icns entries in a different order. The pictures are the same and the test passes on both, but the doc sentence is wrong. Suggested wording: 'the same pictures; icon.icns may differ in entry order'.

The suggested U-entry check step does not match what Android shows. It says 'On Android ... round launchers: the tile in a circle'. AndroidManifest.xml has android:icon="@mipmap/ic_launcher" and no android:roundIcon, so ic_launcher_round.png (and ic_launcher_foreground.png, which only an adaptive-icon XML would use) is never shown. Drop the round-launcher clause from the 'Check in the app' text, or say the round file is kept but unused.

Android 8+ adaptive icon: this is not a regression (the base had no mipmap-anydpi-v26 either). Without one, a Pixel-style launcher may shrink the legacy square tile into its own white shape. The fixer correctly removed the CLI's adaptive set (white #FFFFFF background) and listed this as an owner question. Keep it as an open question for the owner. Base and head also both keep the stale template drawables res/drawable/ic_launcher_background.xml and res/drawable-v24/ic_launcher_foreground.xml, which nothing references.

apps/approvals-web (the web fallback a person opens in a browser) still has no favicon. Its index.html has no <link rel="icon">. That is outside this task (item 2 names apps/ui only), but it is the same class of gap. Worth a follow-up: base './' there, so href="./favicon.svg" plus a public/favicon.svg copy, with a matching case in scripts/app-icon.test.ts.

No test ties the shipped pixels to the master render itself. How the runtime icon is chosen: tauri-codegen 2.7.3 on Linux uses the first listed PNG (icons/32x32.png). On Windows it calls tauri 2.12.4's default_window_icon_from_app_icon_resource, which loads the exe's icon resource at the system's icon size. So the new ico frame order (16 first; the stock had 32 first) does not change which frame the window or tray uses.

Running dot: I reimplemented with_running_dot (r = 22%, ring = r + 6%, DOT [37,99,235], RING white) over the new 32x32.png and looked at it on light and dark backgrounds. The blue disc with its white ring is clearly visible at the lower right; it covers the kite's lower-right facets and the kite still reads. tray::tests::the_running_dot_is_drawn_at_the_lower_right_over_the_icon passes.
